content: The contributors to this guideline provided information that was reviewed, and it was determined that there were no conflicts of interest among the individuals involved in its development. Guideline Development Group 1. Members of the Guideline Development Group Obumneme Ezeanosike: Affiliated with Alex Ekwueme Federal University Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, Nigeria. Male. Expertise in pediatrics, pharmacology, and neonatology. No conflicts of interest declared. Shakilu Jumanne Kayungo: Affiliated with the University of Dodoma and Benjamin Mkapa Hospital, Dodoma, Tanzania. Male. Expertise in pediatric hematology and oncology. No conflicts of interest declared. Winifrida Mwashala: Affiliated with St. Lucia Nursing Home, Arusha, Tanzania. Female. Expertise in nursing and home-based care. No conflicts of interest declared. Eve Namisango: Affiliated with the African Palliative Care Association and the African Centre for Systematic Reviews and Knowledge Translation, College of Medicine, Makerere University, Uganda. Female. Expertise in pain outcomes and HIV-related pain. No conflicts of interest declared. Linda Marisol Bustamante Tuchez: Affiliated with Unidad Nacional de Oncología Pediátrica, Guatemala City, Guatemala. Female. Expertise in pediatric palliative care and pediatric oncology. No conflicts of interest declared. Diederik de Savorin Lohman: Affiliated with Open Society Foundations and Human Rights Watch, New Jersey, USA. Male. Expertise in health and human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. Megan Doherty: Affiliated with the Children’s Hospital of Eastern Ontario, Ottawa, Canada. Female. Expertise in pediatric palliative care and humanitarian settings. No conflicts of interest declared. Andrew Kolodny: Affiliated with Brandeis University, Heller School of Social Policy and Management, Massachusetts, USA. Male. Expertise in access and regulation of medicines. President and Director of Physicians for Responsible Opioid Prescribing (PROP), unpaid roles. PROP does not accept funding from commercial entities and advocates for increased U.S. government regulation of pharmaceutical companies. C. Meghan McMurtry: Affiliated with the University of Guelph and McMaster Children’s Hospital, Guelph, Canada. Female. Expertise in psychology and pediatric chronic pain. No conflicts of interest declared. Justin Mariana Yagam: Affiliated with the Northern Ontario School of Medicine and Solutions for Kids in Pain (SKIP), Yellowknife, Canada. Female. Expertise in patient perspectives. No conflicts of interest declared. Maha Atout: Affiliated with the Nursing School, Philadelphia University, Amman, Jordan. Female. Expertise in pediatric palliative care nursing and communication with children with life-threatening conditions. No conflicts of interest declared. Hibah Osman: Affiliated with the American University of Beirut Medical Center, Lebanon. Female. Expertise in family medicine, hospice, and palliative medicine. Executive Director of Balsam Lebanese Center for Palliative Care (up to July 2018, $4000/month). Current board member of the International Association of Hospice and Palliative Care (IAHPC) (2019–2021). Franca Benini: Affiliated with the Department of Women’s and Children’s Health, University of Padua, Italy. Female. Expertise in pediatric palliative care, neonatology, and pharmacology. No conflicts of interest declared. Jane Emily Harrop: Affiliated with Helen and Douglas House, Oxford University Hospitals, UK. Female. Expertise in pediatric palliative care and neurobiology of infant pain. UK NICE advisory committee member. No conflicts of interest declared. Satbir Jassal: Affiliated with Rainbows Hospice for Children and Young Adults, Leicestershire, UK. Male. Expertise in pediatric palliative care. No conflicts of interest declared. Rhiannon Joslin: Affiliated with Western Sussex Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Southampton, UK. Female. Expertise in physiotherapy and chronic pain in children. No conflicts of interest declared. Bridgit Toebes: Affiliated with the University of Groningen, Faculty of Law, Netherlands. Female. Expertise in human rights laws and the right to health. No conflicts of interest declared. Ben Gal Yael: Affiliated with Schneider Children’s Medical Center of Israel, Clalit Health Organization, Tel Aviv, Israel. Female. Expertise in oncology nursing and policy advocacy. No conflicts of interest declared. Gayatri Palat: Affiliated with MNJ Institute of Oncology and Regional Cancer Centre, Hyderabad, India. Female. Expertise in palliative medicine. No conflicts of interest declared. M.R. Rajagopal: Affiliated with the Trivandrum Institute of Palliative Sciences, Kerala, India. Male. Expertise in palliative medicine and anesthesiology. No conflicts of interest declared. Leonila Dans: Affiliated with the University of the Philippines – Manila, Philippines. Female. Expertise in pediatric rheumatology and clinical epidemiology. No conflicts of interest declared. Susan Lord: Affiliated with John Hunter Children’s Hospital, Hunter Medical Research Institute, University of Newcastle, Australia. Female. Expertise in anesthesia and pain medicine. No conflicts of interest declared. Teck Chuan Voo: Affiliated with the Centre for Biomedical Ethics, National University of Singapore, Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, Singapore. Male. Expertise in biomedical ethics and public health ethics. No conflicts of interest declared. Nobuyuki Yotani: Affiliated with the National Center for Child Health and Development, Tokyo, Japan. Male. Expertise in pediatric palliative care. No conflicts of interest declared. (Co-chairs of the guideline development group.) External Review Group 2. Members of the External Review Group Rashmi Bhandari: Affiliated with the Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine, Stanford University Medical Center, USA. Female. Expertise in clinical psychology, pediatric pain management, and academia. No conflicts of interest declared. Helen Foster: Affiliated with Newcastle University, UK. Female. Expertise in pediatric rheumatology and clinical pain management. No conflicts of interest declared. Tracy Hagemann: Affiliated with the University of Tennessee, College of Pharmacy, USA. Female. Expertise in pediatric pharmacy, pediatric pain management, and academia. Paid speaker for professional body conferences (2006–2014). Jane Nakawesi: Affiliated with Mildmay Hospital, Kampala, Uganda. Female. Expertise in pediatrics, clinical pain management in children, rehabilitation, and palliative care. No conflicts of interest declared. Joshua Pate: Affiliated with the University of Technology Sydney, Australia. Male. Expertise in physiotherapy, pediatric pain, and academia. No conflicts of interest declared. Rikard Wicksell: Associate professor at Karolinska Institute, Stockholm, Sweden. Male. Expertise in clinical psychology and pediatric chronic pain. Received a research grant from AFA Insurance (€340,000, 2015–2018) for developing and evaluating a digital behavioral intervention for chronic pain. WHO Steering Group 3. Members of the Steering Group Department Directors and Focal Persons: Maternal, newborn, child, adolescent health, and aging: Anshu Banerjee, Pura Rayco-Solon, Ayesha de Costa, Bernadette Daelmans, Zeea Han, Yuka Sumi. Noncommunicable diseases: Etienne Krug, Cherian Varghese. Mental health and substance abuse: Devora Kestel, Lillia Dilkushi Poovendran, Vladimir Poznyak, Tarun Dua. Access to medicines and health products: Mariângela Simão, Gilles Forte. Integrated health services: Edward Kelley, Marie-Charlotte Bouesseau. African Region: Felicitas Zawaira, Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo. (Responsible technical officers.) Observers and Methodologists Jo Wilmshurst: President, International Child Neurology Association. Dr. Nandi Siegfried: Consultant, Cape Town, South Africa. Systematic Review Teams The Cochrane Pain, Palliative and Supportive Care (PaPas) group, Cochrane Qualitative Implementation Methods Group (QIMG), and Cochrane Response team conducted systematic reviews of evidence. Quantitative evidence review led by Dr. Emma Fisher. Qualitative evidence review led by Dr. Emma France. Economist: Dr. James Hawkins, National Guideline Alliance, UK. Web Annexes Annex A: Processes and methods for guideline development. Annex B: Summary of methods for systematic reviews of effectiveness and qualitative evidence. Annex C–K: Detailed results and characteristics of systematic reviews on physical therapy, psychological therapy, pharmacological therapy, qualitative evidence, and economic studies.
